Owner-approved reject-without-audit-writes: Go audits schema-invalid calls; Rust writes no rejected-call invocation record. The Rust contract fingerprints every database row.

Owner-approved refuse-before-operation-record: Go persists an operation row for a task-aware call before DispatchTool resolves its binding (internal/hostmcp/server.go:1644-1652), so a call refused at admission leaves a row and breaks X2; Rust records nothing durable for it. The wire task and its typed error are unchanged. The Rust contract fingerprints every database row.
The approved refusal contract omits precisely the refused task handle operation row in Rust. X2 independently requires Rust tables to be empty; no admitted row is exempted.

Rust's redact_for_storage (redact-unmarked-projections) replaces every unmarked/open-schema leaf under a durable row's structured content with the literal "[redacted]", recursively, regardless of field name or depth -- get_host_info's capacity/system/rootDiskQuota, get_vm_info's state, and similar open diagnostic objects across other capabilities' structured observations. Go's pinned reference persists the real value at the same positions; this is the declared, unchanged baseline, not a parity gap. dropValueDeep removes any such redacted leaf from both sides, converging them before comparison.
